name: Ibn Khaldun — dynastic cycle
short_description: ~120-year asabiyyah cycle: founding → prosperity → luxury → decline → collapse
reference_peak_rationale: French Revolution as proxy for old-order asabiyyah crumbling — a late-stage collapse point anchored at the start of a new cycle

name: Kondratiev wave
short_description: ~50–60 year long economic wave: technological expansion → plateau → stagnation → trough
reference_peak_rationale: Top of the post-WWII K-wave, marked by the oil shock and end of the Bretton Woods system
source: Nikolai Kondratiev, The Major Economic Cycles (1925); reinterpreted by Schumpeter and later scholars

name: Huntington — creedal passion
short_description: ~60-year cycle of American political moralism: reform surges followed by cynical intervals
reference_peak_rationale: Civil-rights-era creedal-passion peak per Huntington, American Politics: The Promise of Disharmony (1981)
source: Samuel P. Huntington, American Politics: The Promise of Disharmony (1981)

name: Carlota Perez — techno-economic paradigm
short_description: ~50-60 year wave: installation phase (frenzy + bubble) → turning point → deployment phase (synergy + maturity)
reference_peak_rationale: Dot-com bubble peak, end of installation phase of the ICT paradigm per Perez (2002)
source: Carlota Perez, Technological Revolutions and Financial Capital (2002)

name: Peter Turchin — secular cycles
short_description: ~150-year cycles of elite overproduction → immiseration → state breakdown → reconsolidation
reference_peak_rationale: Turchin's published 'Ages of Discord' prediction of US instability peaking in the 2020s, anchored to forecasts in End Times (2023)
source: Peter Turchin, Secular Cycles (2009), Ages of Discord (2016), End Times (2023)

name: Ray Dalio — Big Cycle
short_description: ~75-100 year cycle of imperial rise/fall: rising → top → declining → reset, tracking debt, currency reserve status, and internal order
reference_peak_rationale: Peak of US empire by Dalio's composite index, end of WWII consolidating reserve-currency dominance, per Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order (2021)
source: Ray Dalio, Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order (2021)

name: Strauss-Howe — saeculum
short_description: ~80-90 year saeculum: high → awakening → unraveling → crisis (4th turning), driven by generational replacement
reference_peak_rationale: Onset of Strauss-Howe's predicted Fourth Turning, anchored to the 2008 financial crisis per The Fourth Turning (1997)
source: William Strauss & Neil Howe, The Fourth Turning (1997)
caveat: Generational theory is contested in academic history. Included for completeness because it's enormously influential in popular discourse. Treat skeptically.
